ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a slanted parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom sides. Inside it are two congruent unshaded regular hexagons. The hexagons share one slanted side, and each hexagon has sides lying along or touching the boundary of the parallelogram. The remaining regions in opposite corners of the parallelogram are shaded gray. Reasoning: Let the side length of each regular hexagon be s. A regular hexagon can be divided into 6 equilateral triangles of side s, so the two identical hexagons together have area equal to 12 such small equilateral triangles. Using the side directions visible in the diagram, the whole parallelogram lies on the same equilateral-triangle/rhombus lattice. From the contacts of the hexagons with the parallelogram sides, the parallelogram spans 4 side-length units in the horizontal direction and 3 side-length units in the slanted direction. Thus it contains 4 × 3 = 12 unit rhombi, and each unit rhombus equals 2 small equilateral triangles. Therefore the parallelogram has area equal to 24 small equilateral triangles. The two white hexagons occupy 12/24 = 1/2 of the parallelogram, so the shaded remaining area is also 1/2.
